nuxthub: moved database, kv, blob, cache from hub to vitehub with preset "cloudflare", rewrote 11 imports and 3 KV and Blob calls, and moved the schema to server/databases/.
Dry run: no files were written.

Manual follow-ups (15):
  1. wrangler.jsonc:20 The codemod removed migrations_table: "_hub_migrations". NuxtHub and Wrangler record migrations differently, so ViteHub must not reuse that table. Baseline the database instead (see the database follow-ups).
  2. wrangler.jsonc:18 ViteHub writes the DB binding itself, and a binding name alone can point at a new empty resource. To keep this D1 database, set cloudflare: { binding: "DB", databaseId: "a30aa564-d388-493b-8994-23f8dfd129f5" } in defineDatabase() in server/databases/config.ts. ViteHub writes migrations_dir for server/databases/migrations. Then remove this entry from wrangler.jsonc.
  3. wrangler.jsonc:26 ViteHub writes the KV binding itself, and a binding name alone can point at a new empty resource. To keep this namespace, set vitehub.kv to { driver: "cloudflare-kv-binding", binding: "KV", namespaceId: "ba6f3913de344cb1a833f3cf20ba5aa8" } in nuxt.config. Then remove this entry from wrangler.jsonc.
  4. wrangler.jsonc:30 ViteHub writes the CACHE binding itself, and a binding name alone can point at a new empty resource. On Cloudflare, cache: true needs a namespace ID. To keep this namespace, set vitehub.cache to { driver: "cloudflare-kv-binding", binding: "CACHE", namespaceId: "ba6f3913de344cb1a833f3cf20ba5aa8" } in nuxt.config. Then remove this entry from wrangler.jsonc.
  5. wrangler.jsonc:36 ViteHub writes the BLOB binding itself, and a binding name alone can point at a new empty resource. To keep this bucket, set vitehub.blob to { driver: "cloudflare-r2", binding: "BLOB", bucketName: "hub-starter-p2s5" } in nuxt.config. Then remove this entry from wrangler.jsonc.
  6. server/api/images/[pathname].delete.ts:6 blob.del() returns its result to the caller. In ViteHub it resolves to an [error, value] tuple instead of throwing. Check the error, then return the value.
  7. server/api/images/upload.post.ts:4 blob.handleUpload() returns its result to the caller. In ViteHub it resolves to an [error, value] tuple instead of throwing. Check the error, then return the value.
  8. server/api/redirects/index.get.ts:4 kv.get() is used inside an expression. In ViteHub it resolves to an [error, value] tuple instead of the value. Check the error, then use the value.
  9. server/routes/images/[...pathname].get.ts:7 blob.serve() returns its result to the caller. In ViteHub it resolves to an [error, value] tuple instead of throwing. Check the error, then return the value.
  10. Back up the existing database and stop the app. For local SQLite, copy NuxtHub's .data/db/sqlite.db to ViteHub's default location with `mkdir -p .vitehub/data/database && cp .data/db/sqlite.db .vitehub/data/database/sqlite.db`, together with its -wal and -shm files if they exist.
  11. Create the migration baseline with `pnpm vitehub db generate --name baseline`. It writes server/databases/migrations/. Do not copy NuxtHub's server/db/migrations/ there.
  12. Compare the baseline SQL with the existing tables, columns, indexes, and constraints. When they match, replace the whole baseline .sql file with `SELECT 1;`. Keep its file name and the meta/ files.
  13. Run `pnpm nuxt build`, then record the baseline on D1 with `pnpm wrangler d1 migrations apply <database-name> --remote --config .output/server/wrangler.json`. Check first with `migrations list` that only the baseline is pending. For the local SQLite copy, run `pnpm vitehub db migrate`.
  14. Copy the local KV data. Both use the fs-lite driver: `mkdir -p .vitehub/data && cp -R .data/kv .vitehub/data/kv`.
  15. ViteHub stores Blob metadata in another format, so copy each local blob through the API. With the dev server running, run `pnpm vitehub blob put <pathname> .data/blob/<pathname> --content-type <type>` for each file. Custom metadata is not copied.

Notes:
  - vite-hub/nuxt auto-imports kv, blob, db, and schema in server code for each enabled feature, as NuxtHub did.
  - Local data stays in .data/. ViteHub reads .vitehub/data/. The follow-ups list the commands that copy it.
  - NuxtHub's server/db/migrations/ stays in place for reference. ViteHub writes new migrations to server/databases/migrations/ and does not apply them during dev or build. Delete the old folder after the baseline.
  - cachedEventHandler() and defineCachedFunction() come from Nitro, so they keep working with cache: true.

Next steps:
  - Run `pnpm install` to install vite-hub and @vite-hub/database and remove @nuxthub/core.
  - Run `npx nuxi prepare`, then type-check the app.
  - Run `pnpm nuxt build` and `pnpm vitehub inspect provider-output --json` to check the resources and bindings.
